newsitem.title: UK: LME metals mostly slow, trend lower at close.
newsitem.headline: LME metals mostly slow, trend lower at close.

text.p: Base metal trading was mostly low-key on the LME on Thursday, with prices gradually crumbling towards softer closes, traders said.
Copper and aluminium held up relatively well, with losses from Wednesday restricted to single figures, but the other metals came in for moderate speculative selling, they said.
"The day as a whole has been extremely slow, apart from the late sell-off," one trader said.
Late losses in metals such as zinc, lead, tin and nickel reflected disappointed liquidation after earlier failures at overhead resistance levels.
"The spec sales are small-scale. There has been no real fund stuff, and trade business has been slow," he said.

Copper had managed to hold above the $2,300 a tonne level, but given the lack of resolve overhead -- resistance is strong between $2,310 and $2,320 -- the market looked set to test the downside again, traders said.
Last three months business was at $2,302, down just $5 from Wednesday. The cash/threes backwardation eased modestly to $45/47.
Aluminium was unable to clear $1,600, despite an LME stock fall and a drop in February IPAI producer inventories.
Traders said the bullish implications of the latter were negated by the overall sluggish atmosphere in the complex. Prices ended the kerb at $1,586, down $6.
Nickel moved lower from early levels above $7,500, although market liquidity was not great. Last trade was at $7,375, a $115 loss.
Lead and zinc stalled at respective resistance levels in the mid-$650s and mid-$1,260s, but declines were largely confined to the kerb.
Lead ended $12 lower at $639, while zinc finished $22 softer at $1,244.
Tin followed the overall trend, and closed $70 down at $5,690. However, the neglected alloy market was stable at $1,470/75 a tonne.
